ORIGINAL RESEARCH

# Mental arithmetic task load recognition using EEG signal and Bayesian optimized K-nearest neighbor

Lakhan Dev Sharma<sup>1</sup> • Himanshu Chhabra<sup>2</sup> • Urvashi Chauhan<sup>3</sup> • Ritesh Kumar Saraswat<sup>2</sup> • Ramesh Kumar Sunkaria<sup>4</sup>

Received: 18 March 2021 / Accepted: 6 September 2021 / Published online: 6 October 2021

\- Bharati Vidyapeeth’s Institute of Computer Applications and Management 2021

Abstract Cognitive load recognition during mental arithmetic activity facilitates to observe and identify the brain’s response towards stress stimulus. As a result, an efficient mental load characterization approach using electroencephalogram (EEG) signal and Bayesian optimized K-Nearest Neighbor (BO-KNN) has been proposed in this work. The study has been conducted on a recorded EEG dataset of 30 healthy subjects who were exposed to an arithmetic questioner. To obtain artifacts free EEG signal, the Savitzky–Golay filtering approach has been utilized. Further, the decomposition of the extracted EEG signal has been carried out using stationary wavelength transform. In this work, the entropy based feature extraction has been performed followed by F-score based feature selection. Top 40 features having the highest precedence have been used for classification using BO-KNN. The rigorous experimental analysis has been performed to analyze the effectiveness of the proposed method over other state-of-the-art methods and it shows that the classification accuracy is substantially improved.

Keywords Cognitive task - EEG - Stationary wavelet transformation - Bayesian optimized K-nearest neighbor (BO-KNN)

## 1 Introduction

In the current scenario the cognitive load analysis is essential in order to prevent the human from various physiological and psychological disorders such as heart attack, depression & anxiety and seizure etc. Neuroscience has proved that continuous exposure to mental load may affect the brain dynamics [1, 2]. These variations are reflected in the electroencephalography (EEG) signal. Therefore, analysis of EEG signals is often utilized for cognitive load recognition. It is a non-invasive method for cognitive load detection. EEG represents the electrical activity of brain that varies if there is any change occurs in the input conditions. Other physiological markers can only record secondary variations created by the brain, which is the fundamental response source to any environmental input [3]. In this work, such variations in EEG signal under the exposure of stressful activities are detected and analyzed in order to classify the overall brain response into two relevant classes i.e. resting state and stressed or cognitive task performing state [4]. Literature suggests numerous EEG based classification approaches that make significant contribution in medical field [5–9]. Binish Fatimah et. al. [10] have proposed an automatic mental arithmetic task detection technique which measures the difficulty level of performed activity using EEG power spectrum. The process of signal decomposition into several rhythms, such as gamma, beta, alpha, theta and delta, is achieved using a filter bank. Another cognitive task recognition technique has been implemented in [11], where the Fourier decomposition of EEG signal is adopted into uniform frequency bands and Kruskal Wallis approach is used for statistical feature selection. Further Qiang Wang et. al. [12] have developed a fractal dimension spectrum based mental load detection algorithm that monitored the brain response towards the mental arithmetic task. Here several feature like: statistical features, power spectral density, autoregressive model have been analyzed. Pega Zargem et. al. [13] have designed mental load characterizing algorithm that analyzes the brain activity under varying (very low to extreme high) mental arithmetic loads. However, the existing non invasive stress detection techniques need improvements in terms of classification accuracy. Moreover, optimization plays a vital role in determining the tuned algorithm parameters in order to enhance the algorithm accuracy. Therefore, this article presents a novel mental arithmetic load recognition approach using EEG signal and Bayesian optimized K-Nearest Neighbor (BO-KNN). The proposed technique effectively investigates the impact of mental arithmetic tasks on brain dynamics. Extensive experimental analysis has been carried out in order to justify the efficacy of the proposed technique over other state-of-art methods.

## 2 Experimental protocol

The main objective of this study is to investigate the mental load during the arithmetic task activity using EEG signal analysis. For this purpose, the mental arithmetic tasks experiment has been conducted for EEG data recording of 30 healthy subjects with different age groups. In this section the process that we followed for the data collection and organization have been presented.

## 2.1 Data acquisition

In this work, the EEG dataset has been recorded using MP 45 2-channel data acquisition system (BIOPAC) at a sampling frequency of 500 Hz. Here, we have considered a bipolar method to record the EEG signal. In this method, the EEG is recorded from a pair of electrodes placed over the subject’s scalp $( F _ { p 1 }$ and $F _ { p 2 } )$ as per 10–20 EEG electrode placement. A third electrode is attached behind the ear as a point of reference. Electrode placement of a subject is shown in Figure 1. The EEG data from 30 healthy subjects has been recorded. Every recording includes separate artifact-free EEG segments of 900 s for resting state and 300 s for mental counting. Based on EEG visual inspection, 10 of the 30 initial participants were excluded from the database due to poor EEG quality (excessive number of myographic artifacts), so the final sample size is of 20 subjects.

Subjects from different age groups (from 20 to 57 years) and gender are chosen for EEG recording. The participating subjects detail is summarized in Table 1. Male subjects are symbolize with ‘M’ whereas Female are marked with $`` \mathrm{F} ''$ . The data were recorded to analyze the EEG correlate under the exposure of stress in the form of mental arithmetic task performed by the participating subject as it is standard stress introducing experimental protocol. Arithmetic task include the basic arithmetic operations such as addition, subtraction, and multiplication. Before the data recording, subjects are instructed to stay calm and relaxed. The subjects sat on an arm chair in a comfortable position and 5 minu adaptation time was given prior to EEG recording to adapt them in the experimental conditions followed by rest state data recording with closed eyes for next 15 min. The mental arithmetic task is performed for 5 minutes duration, whereas 5 min adaptation time prior to stress questioner is considered. The participants were instructed not to use finger movements for counting. They were informed to perform the arithmetic task mentally, without speaking and without using any other way that involves any physical activity. In this way, an intensive mental activity is performed by the subjects during the EEG data recording. During arithmetic calculation, each question was of 1 marks and score obtained by each candidate is shown in Table 1. Organization of EEG data collection is shown in Figures 2 in graphical form.

## 2.2 Self-assessment of participants

All the data have been recorded after written consent of the participant and they were made aware that this data will be used for research purposes only. Post-data recording, every participant was given a questioner and were asked to give answers on a scale of 1 to 10. These questions were as follows:

Q1: How mentally demanding was the task (Mental Demand).

Q2: How hurried or rushed was the pace of the task (Temporal Demand).

Q3: How successful were you in accomplishing what you were asked to do (Performance).

Q4: How has did you have to work to accomplish your level of performance (Effort).

Q5: How insecure, discouraged, irritated, stressed, and annoying were you (Frustration).

## 3 Proposed methodology

In this work the recorded EEG signal is filtered using the Savitzky–Golay filtering approach to get artifact-free EEG signals. The decomposition of filtered EEG signal has been done using stationary wavelet transform and sample entropy features are extracted and feature selection is made based on F-scare values. The selected features were further used for classification by BO-KNN. Fig 3 depicts the flowchart of the methodology adopted in this work.

## 3.1 Preprocessing using Savitzky- Golay filter

In this work, a Savitzky–Golay (SG) smoothing filter is used to eliminate the artifacts. The Savitzky–Golay filter is the general form of the FIR filter that optimally fit the set of data points to a polynomial in least squares sense [14, 15]. Here the assumption have made that $2m + 1 \quad (i.e. -$ m $t o \mathrm { ~ } + m )$ data points are places symmetrically about the origin $( i . e .   m = 0 )$ given as follows.

$$
X = [ x _ {- m}, x _ {- m + 1}, \dots , x _ {m} ] ^ {T}\tag{1}
$$

In this method the dth orders of differentiation of dataset at origin $( m = 0 )$ is obtained by performing the differentiation on fitted pth order polynomial instead of original set of data. Orders of filter have been considered as in [16].

## 3.2 Decomposition using stationary wavelet transform

The decomposition of EEG signal into various frequency bands has been accomplished using stationary wavelet transform (SWT) which facilitates analysis of time-domain EEG signal [17]. One of the primary benefits of wavelets is that they allow for simultaneous localization in the time and frequency domains. The ability of wavelets to distinguish tiny features in a signal is a significant benefit. SWT carries the same temporal information at every segmented level and offers time-invariant property. Here the actual data is not decimated [18]. The high-pass and low-pass filters used at every stage are modified by adding the zeros [19]. In this work 5th order Daubechies wavelet have been used with 6 levels of decomposition.

## 3.3 Sample entropy based feature extraction

Entropy is a nonlinear measure that indicates the degree of chaos of systems [20]. It analyzes the system complexity and random dynamics of nonlinear signals [21, 22]. These measures have shown their effectiveness in understanding the complex dynamical behavior of the brain [23]. Sample Entropy $\mathit { S E N } ( m ,   r ,   P )$ is more reliable for short dataset, also it is less sensitive to the changes in data length [24]. In this work, $\mathit { S E N } ( m ,   r ,   P )$ features have been extracted in order to examine the complexity of time-series signals. Sample entropy is the negative logarithmic of the condition probability that two sequences which have resemblance for m points retain their similarity at the next point $m + 1$ as well. To compute the SEN two essential parameters, tolerance factor r and run length m must be specified. In the present work, tolerance is considered as 0.2 times the standard deviation of segmented signal, whereas m is chosen as {2, 3, 4, 5}. The sample entropy does not include the self matches while determining the probability thus reduces the biasing [20].

The entropy SEN(m, r, P) is evaluated as follows:

$$
S E N (m, r, P) = - \log \frac {A ^ {m}}{B ^ {m}}\tag{2}
$$

## 3.4 Feature selection using Fisher score

The precedence evaluation of extracted features is necessary in order to obtain accurate classification with less complexity. Therefore, in this work, the top 40 features are selected on the basis of Fisher score (F-score) measure [22]. The mathematical expression that represents the F score calculation of jth feature is given as follows:

$$
F ^ {j} = \frac {\sum_ {k = 1} ^ {a} n _ {k} (\mu_ {k} ^ {j} - \mu^ {j}) ^ {2}}{(\sigma^ {j}) ^ {2}}\tag{3}
$$

Where $\sigma ^ { j }$ and $\mu ^ { j }$ denote the standard deviation and mean value respectively. a represents the class, whereas $n _ { k }$ is the number of instances in kth class. The mean value of jth feature of kth class is denoted by $\mu _ { k } ^ { j }$ . The feature having the highest F score value is considered the most discriminating feature.

## 3.5 Classification using K-nearest neighbors (KNN)

In the present work the selected features have been classified using supervised machine learning based classifier i.e. KNN. KNN is a non parametric classification technique where the member of training set nearest to test sample has been identified by calculating distance function [25, 26]. KNN technique offers simple and easy implementation without considering the assumptions [27].

## 3.6 Hyper-parameter tuning using Bayesian optimization algorithm (BOA)

Machine learning algorithms are rarely parameter-free. Bayesian optimization algorithm [28] provides an elegant approach and has been shown to outperform other state-of-the-art global optimization algorithms on a number of challenging optimization benchmark functions [29]. BOA attempts to minimize a scalar objective function $f ( x )$ for x in a bounded domain. In this work, BOA has been used to optimally select the tuning parameters of KNN on which its performance largely depends.

## 4 Mental arithmetic task load recognition experimentation results

Experiments were performed in MATLAB 2019b on Intel i7 processor with 16GB RAM using Windows 10 operating system. To overcome the possibility of bias in results, 10-fold cross-validation has been performed. Distance metrics, distance weight, and $\mathrm { { } ^ { \circ } K ^ { \prime } }$ are important tuning parameters of KNN on which its performance depends. The parameter $\mathrm { { } ^ { \circ } K ^ { \prime } }$ in KNN refers to the number of closest neighbors to include in the voting process. Distance metrics are a mathematical formula used to calculate distance in machine learning models. These key parameters of KNN have been tuned and optimized using Bayesian optimization and error minimization curve is shown in Figure 4.

Figure 5 shows the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC curve) for mental arithmetic task load recognition. Two parameters plotted on this curve are: False Positive Rate and True Positive Rate. Area under the ROC Curve (AUC) is a measurement of the entire two-dimensional area beneath the entire ROC curve. It is a composite measure of performance that takes into account all possible classification thresholds. The AUC value ranges from 0 to 1. AUC of a model whose predictions are 100 percent correct is 1.0. For the proposed model, AUC was obtained to be 0.97 and an overall classification accuracy (Ac%) of 96.07 % has been achieved.

This model outperform the other methods based on non-linear features and ML based classification [4, 30, 31]. ## 6 Conclusion

In this work, a novel approach for cognitive load detection during mental arithmetic task has been implemented using EEG signal and BO-KNN classifier. The experimentation has been done on the EEG data set of 20 individuals. The data is recorded during the resting state and while performing some mental arithmetic task. For the preprocessing, the Savitzky–Golay filter is used and SWT is used for the signal decomposition. Here, sample entropy features are extracted and classified using BO-KNN. The result analysis shows that the, overall accuracy of 96.07% has been achieved using this method, which is higher than the existing state-of-art techniques.

Future scope: Following are future scope for research in this filed.

Effect of filtering can be studied: EEG is nonstationary and susceptible to a variety of noises. Removing noise can be a critical topic for EEG researchers.

Emotional states can be analyzed: Study of emotional states with respect to different external stimuli can be done.

Leave-one-out validation: To eliminate the possibility of bias, this study used 10-fold cross-validation. Leaveone-out validation can be performed for an algorithm to test on a more real-life situation.

Wide validation: In this experiment, EEG recordings from 30 subjects were used. For more generic results, this work can be extended to a larger database.
